bull.t: Rapid revenue growth & improving gross margin
bull.b: Revenue accelerated materially from 2024 into the TTM period while gross margin improved to ~40%, showing product-market fit and the ability to scale revenue without proportionate gross cost increases. This durable top-line expansion and margin recovery support longer-term operating leverage as sales scale.

bull.t: Contract backlog and defined revenue streams
bull.b: An $800M tokenization backlog tied to roughly $90M of fees provides multi-period revenue visibility as projects are funded. Management also defines licensing, tokenization fees and exchange monetization as distinct streams, which diversify durable cash generation beyond one-off deals.

bull.t: Low leverage and improved equity base
bull.b: The balance sheet shows very low financial leverage and a materially improved equity position versus prior years, giving financial flexibility. Low debt reduces bankruptcy and interest risk, supporting capital deployment and partner confidence during a multi‑quarter scale-up phase.

bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow on a TTM basis indicate the business is not yet self-funding; sustained cash burn erodes runway and forces reliance on external capital. Over multiple quarters this raises dilution risk and constrains reinvestment or margin improvement without successful funding execution.

bear.t: Deep unprofitability and negative operating margins
bear.b: Extremely negative operating and net margins show operating costs far outstrip revenue today. That structural loss profile means the company must materially improve cost structure or scale high‑margin revenue rapidly; otherwise returns on capital will remain negative and investor reliance on financing will persist.

bear.t: Material dilution and governance risk from financing
bear.b: A large structured financing term sheet carries the risk of substantial equity dilution and incremental board/control rights for the counterparty. Such outcomes could alter strategic direction, reduce existing shareholders’ economic interests and complicate long-term governance, limiting management flexibility during scaling.
